about: A bus captain’s first route of the day

lines.text: Long before most of the city wakes, Mdm Lee is already at work.
She has drove the first bus out of the depot for eleven years.
lines.note: Verb form: after 'has' it is 'driven', not 'drove'.

lines.text: Her alarm rings at half past three, and she reach the depot by
four. Before setting off, she checks the tyres, the mirrors and the doors.
The roads are almost empty at that hour, so the route is never
lines.note: Connector: the two ideas contrast, so it is 'but', not 'so'.

lines.text: lonely. Her earliest passengers are cleaners, nurses and bakers which start work before
dawn. She knows many of them by name and greets them warm.
lines.note: Word form: 'greets' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'warmly'.

lines.text: One old man has brought her coffee every morning since many years.
lines.note: Preposition: a length of time takes 'for'; 'since' needs a starting point.

lines.text: Last month, when a schoolboy leaves his wallet on a seat, she handed
lines.note: Tense: it happened last month, so it is 'left'.

lines.text: it in at the office herself. Driving safely, she says, matters far more
than driving fast. By sunrise, she has already completed a entire trip, and
lines.note: Article: 'entire' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an entire trip'.

lines.text: her passengers have reached their workplaces safely and on time.
